restriction: Permitted as a preservative in cosmetic products only within the stated limits.

hazard: Haematotoxicity is described as a predominant toxicological feature of 2-phenoxyethanol in vivo and in vitro. Rabbits were the most sensitive species tested. The main metabolite, 2-phenoxyacetic acid, may accumulate in the kidney and may be responsible for kidney toxicity in rats after oral exposure.
opinion: Using an adjusted NOAEL of 357 mg/kg bw/day from a 90-day dermal study in rabbits and aggregate exposure for preservatives in cosmetics, a Margin of Safety (MoS) of 130 was derived for adults, against a minimum MoS of 25 selected by the SCCS. The SCCS states this span also covers the safety of infants and babies. For children up to 3 years, exposure may be higher than for adults, but MoS values from reasonable worst-case scenarios are considered sufficient (e.g. MoS of 41 with the EFSA 7 kg default body weight).
conditions: Assessment is based on dermal exposure and aggregate exposure to preservatives in cosmetics. The concentration limit is not stated in this excerpt.
source_quote: Using an adjusted NOAEL of 357 mg/kg bw/day from a 90-day dermal RDT study in rabbits and the aggregate exposure for preservatives in cosmetics, for adult humans a MoS of 130 was derived.
